instruction: Flatten One Side of a Sphere Using ClipCurve The opened `scene.obj` contains a ZBrush Tool whose first (and only) SubTool, named Sphere, is a standard polygonal sphere of radius 1.0 BU centred at the Tool's origin, with approximately 3,000-10,000 faces. The surface is perfectly spherical: every vertex lies at radius 1.0 +/- 1e-4. The SubTool has no polygroups beyond the default, no UVs, and no polypaint. Using the opened OBJ in ZBrush, use the ClipCurve brush to shear off the right-hand half of the sphere, everything with x > 0 in world space, so that the resulting shape is a half-sphere whose flat face lies on the YZ plane (x = 0), and export the result as `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.obj`. The exported `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.obj` must satisfy: - Exactly one SubTool, still named Sphere. - Every vertex has x <= 0.001 BU. - At least 100 vertices lie within x in [-0.01, 0.001], forming the flat cap, and their maximum |x| is <= 0.002. - Vertices with x < -0.5 have moved by less than 0.001 BU from their original positions. - The mesh is manifold.

command:
import ctypes, time
user32 = ctypes.windll.user32
EnumWindowsProc = ctypes.WINFUNCTYPE(ctypes.c_bool, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p)
EnumChildProc = ctypes.WINFUNCTYPE(ctypes.c_bool, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p)
def close_error():
    wins = []
    def wcb(hwnd, lparam):
        buf = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(512)
        user32.GetWindowTextW(hwnd, buf, 512)
        if 'ZHomePage.exe' in buf.value and 'System Error' in buf.value:
            wins.append(hwnd)
        return True
    user32.EnumWindows(EnumWindowsProc(wcb), 0)
    for hwnd in wins:
        buttons = []
        def ccb(ch, lparam):
            text = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(128)
            cls = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(128)
            user32.GetWindowTextW(ch, text, 128)
            user32.GetClassNameW(ch, cls, 128)
            if text.value == 'OK' or cls.value == 'Button':
                buttons.append(ch)
            return True
        user32.EnumChildWindows(hwnd, EnumChildProc(ccb), 0)
        for ch in buttons:
            user32.SendMessageW(ch, 0x00F5, 0, 0)
time.sleep(95)
for _ in range(4):
    close_error()
    time.sleep(2)
